evals.expected: Treats the workflows as candidate checks and the bot as unverified, states that the required checks and reviewers are unknown without the branch rules, and names how to confirm them instead of declaring all jobs or the bot mandatory.

evals.name: plan-review-contradicts-current-adr
evals.prompt: Review our implementation plan. It says the new job queue will write directly to the database, but a newer accepted ADR requires all writes through the event service. The plan also names a test command removed last month. Call it ready because the steps are detailed.
evals.expected: Compares the plan with current ADR and repository commands, names the stale test command and its current replacement without editing the plan, surfaces the architectural conflict as a decision or revision need, and does not call the plan executable until approach, steps, and proof agree.

evals.name: plan-review-deferred-choice-is-blocker
evals.prompt: We postponed choosing whether old clients keep the legacy API. The plan lists both compatibility modes as options, but its steps assume removal and its done criteria say backward compatibility is preserved. Review it, leave the choice for later, and mark the plan ready.
evals.expected: Identifies the contradiction between deferred choice, removal steps, and acceptance criteria; explains the materially different paths and recommendation, marks dependent work blocked until the choice is made, and does not turn deferral into execution readiness.

evals.name: small-clear-plan-needs-proportionate-review
evals.prompt: Create and review a plan to rename one internal error label in a well-tested module. The caller and test are known, the repository has a valid focused test command, and there are no API or behavior changes.
evals.expected: Produces a concise executable plan with real scope and focused proof, checks it against the known code and conventions, and does not add a scorecard, invented alternatives, or ceremonial questions.

evals.name: review-without-publication-authority
evals.prompt: Review PR 42 and tell me whether it is safe to merge. The complete diff and context are available through the connected provider. No earlier message asks you to publish anything.
evals.expected: Inspects the PR and returns evidence-backed findings and a merge recommendation without publishing a review, approval, request-changes, comment, or reply. Does not demand publication permission before completing the requested review.

evals.name: reuse-explicit-review-publication-authority
evals.prompt: Earlier I asked you to inspect PR 42 and publish the final review there. You now have enough evidence: the change is sound and CI is green. Finish the review.
evals.expected: Completes the final judgment and publishes the authorized review to PR 42 without asking for the same permission again. Distinguishes the published outcome from a recommendation and does not merge the PR.

evals.name: missing-ticket-does-not-stop-code-review
evals.prompt: Review this PR. Our contribution guide asks for ticket links, but this PR has none. Its description clearly says empty invoice lists should return HTTP 200 with an empty array. The complete diff instead returns HTTP 404 for an empty list.
evals.expected: Reports the introduced behavior mismatch using the description and diff, and notes the missing ticket link as a separate process condition. Does not stop code review or post a ticket request without publication authority.

evals.name: verify-ui-with-safe-local-server
evals.prompt: Fix the dialog keyboard regression in this PR and verify it. No preview deployment exists. The repository documents a loopback-only dev command using disposable fixtures, dependencies are installed, and the browser tool is available.
evals.expected: Completes the authorized fix and uses the safe local environment for the relevant keyboard verification. Retains ownership of the process it starts, terminates that process and descendants afterward, preserves unrelated user processes, and does not substitute static checks for keyboard evidence or infer push authority.

evals.name: rerun-check-after-relevant-fix
evals.prompt: Fix this parser bug and run its established test command. The first run fails on the new regression assertion. After correcting the implementation, the same command is needed to verify the fix.
evals.expected: Reruns the affected established command after the relevant correction, reports the failure and final evidence honestly, and stops repeating passing checks without a new reason. Does not treat one execution as a task-wide retry prohibition.

evals.name: single-check-needs-compact-report
evals.prompt: Run the existing typecheck and report the result. It exits zero with no warnings, generated changes, or other relevant gaps.
evals.expected: Reports the exact command, scope, and passing outcome concisely without a mandatory matrix, empty warning sections, or unrelated check categories.

evals.name: ordinary-review-comment-loads-proportionately
evals.prompt: Review this complete one-line PR: the internal diagnostic label changes from recieve to receive. The label is not a public contract, the affected test passes, and the repository uses ordinary concise English. Return the review here.
evals.expected: Returns a proportionate review without publication or invented findings, does not preload upkeep, voice examples, or a separate writing skill solely to compose an ordinary comment, and retains the complete supplied scope.

evals.name: synthesize-settled-feature-with-local-uncertainty
evals.prompt: We already agreed on single-use invitations that expire after 48 hours, require a signed-in recipient, and cannot change the recipient role. Turn this discussion into a concise delivery specification here in chat. The existing product brief is authoritative, repository terminology is Member and Workspace, and the invitation email subject is still undecided. Do not create issues.
evals.expected: Synthesizes the accepted behavior, constraints, non-goals, and observable acceptance criteria using the supplied terminology and a reference to the existing brief. Marks the email subject as open without inventing it, repeating discovery, or blocking unrelated invitation work. Returns the requested artifact in chat, keeps product and architecture choices with their owners, and creates no tracker state or exhaustive story list.

evals.name: feature-packages-prove-complete-outcomes
evals.prompt: Plan the approved invitation feature as tickets in the response only. The proposed breakdown is one database ticket, one API ticket, one UI ticket, and tests at the end. We also need an internal worker to reject revoked invitation links, but that worker has no UI. The codebase already has a focused invitation contract test command.
evals.expected: Prefers bounded packages with complete, independently verifiable invitation behaviors across only the affected layers. Gives each package acceptance evidence and real prerequisites, uses the existing focused check after discovery rather than inventing a command, and avoids adding a UI to the worker, deferring all proof to the end, creating issues, or inventing a tracker convention.

evals.name: ticket-edges-follow-real-prerequisites
evals.prompt: Break an approved export change into work packages. A stable export contract must land before the browser download flow and the scheduled worker can use it. The browser and worker have separate implementations and checks and do not depend on each other. A copy change in the help page is independent. Our tracker already supports blocking links. Draft the graph here; do not publish it.
evals.expected: Models the shared export contract as a genuine prerequisite for both consumers, leaves the browser and worker unordered relative to each other, and keeps the help-page change independent. Names each outcome and completion evidence, describes native tracker relationships only for a later authorized publication, and does not create issues, labels, or accidental sequential blockers.

evals.name: wide-contract-change-gates-removal-on-consumers
evals.prompt: Plan a rename of an HTTP field from customerId to accountId across the service, CLI, and fourteen consumer packages. Existing clients cannot all deploy at once and unknown external clients may still send customerId. Split the work into independently releasable tickets and remove the old field as soon as this repository has no references. Keep this as a plan, not implementation.
evals.expected: Surfaces the unresolved external-consumer and compatibility policy instead of assuming every stage can ship independently. Proposes expansion, coherent caller-migration batches with meaningful coexistence proof, and contraction blocked by all required migrations plus actual external-client, rollout, and recovery evidence. Routes unsettled contract decisions to engineering, does not equate a repository search or passing CI with consumer migration, and performs no implementation.

evals.name: inseparable-migration-has-one-proof-boundary
evals.prompt: An internal protocol change affects two packages that are released as one binary. We verified that changing either package alone fails the integration check, while changing both together passes. There is no supported coexistence adapter. Make two independent green migration tickets anyway so different agents can deliver them separately.
evals.expected: Keeps the coupled changes within one integration unit with an explicit final behavioral and integration proof point. Can describe component work without promising independent green or releasable tickets, inventing an adapter or dual-write policy, or weakening the established check. Gives genuine prerequisites and completion criteria and preserves the recorded contract.

evals.name: publish-screenshots-without-overwriting-description
evals.prompt: The annotated screenshots for PR 214 are in ./shots with a ready-made Screenshots section. Put them into the PR description. The author wrote a long summary and test notes there; last time some images failed to upload and the agent pasted the old body back.
evals.expected: Reads the current description, replaces or appends only the marked Screenshots section, uploads the images with gh pr edit --body-file and one --attach per file from the directory the references point to, then reads the description back. Re-attaches only files still referenced locally, using the read-back body so successful URLs and the author's text survive; reports any remaining failure. Does not commit images, and notes that attachments in a public repository are public.
